title: Keratin Model Parameter Provenance & Epistemic Audit

literature_sources.citation: Phillips, D. G. (1985). Effects of water on the thermal transitions of wool and silk. Polymer, 26(10), 1433-1436.
literature_sources.conditions: Wool fibers, dry state (conditioned over P2O5), heating rate 10-20 C/min

literature_sources.citation: Wortmann, F. J., Rigby, B. J., & Phillips, D. G. (1984). Glass transition temperature of wool. Textile Research Journal, 54(1), 6-8.

Tg0_dry.notes: 145 C represents an underestimate for completely anhydrous wool keratin (which transitions between 160 C and 175 C). 145 C approximates keratin retaining ~1-2% residual bound water or lower crosslink density horn keratin.

kappa_ss.notes: Hypothesized linear shift of Tg with cystine mol% relative to standard wool (7.0 mol%). No direct empirical calorimetric series exists measuring dTg/d[SS] in isolated keratin matrices under matched hydration. Marked strictly as MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS.

literature_sources.reported_value: Initial slope dTg/dw ~ -500 to -800 C / (g/g) for w < 0.10

lambda_water_linear.notes: Linear slope of -750 C/(g/g) is valid strictly for tangent approximation at low hydration (w < 0.08). At w = 0.35 (saturation), it yields unphysical Tg = -116.2 C (157 K), whereas empirical water-saturated keratin Tg asymptotes at -10 C to -25 C. Replaced by the Fox equation.

Tg_fox_dry_keratin.notes: Dry keratin reference temperature in the classic Fox plasticization equation.

literature_sources.citation: Johari, G. P., Hallbrucker, A., & Mayer, E. (1987). The glass-liquid transition of hyperquenched glassy water. Nature, 330, 552-553.

Tg_fox_water.notes: Glass transition temperature of pure amorphous solid water.

literature_sources.citation: Feughelman, M. (1997). Mechanical Properties and Structure of Alpha-keratin Fibres: Wool, Human Hair and Related Fibres. UNSW Press.
literature_sources.reported_value: 0.40 - 0.50 volume fraction of microfibrils (IF) in cortex

literature_sources.citation: Kasapi, M. A., & Gosline, J. M. (1997). Design complexity and fracture toughness of equine hoof wall. J. Exp. Biol., 200, 1639-1659.

phi_IF.notes: Volume fraction of crystalline intermediate filaments embedded in the amorphous disulfide-rich matrix.

literature_sources.citation: Feughelman, M. (1997); Hearle, J. W. S. (2000). A critical review of the structural mechanics of wool and hair fibres. Int. J. Biol. Macromol., 27(2), 123-138.
literature_sources.reported_value: 4.0 - 4.5 GPa dry axial modulus of isolated microfibrils

E_IF_axial.notes: Axial Young's modulus of alpha-helical intermediate filaments. Insensitive to water below 80 C.

E_matrix_dry.notes: Anhydrous modulus of the isotropic sulfur-rich amorphous keratin matrix.

literature_sources.reported_value: 10 - 50 MPa in fully swollen state (rubbery plateau above Tg)

E_matrix_wet.notes: Hydrated rubbery plateau modulus of the matrix when fully plasticized by water.

literature_sources.citation: Gibson, L. J., & Ashby, M. F. (1997). Cellular Solids: Structure and Properties (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.
literature_sources.reported_value: E/E_s = (1 - p)^2 for isotropic open-cell foams or axial pore alignment

porosity_exponent.notes: Gibson-Ashby power law exponent for cellular/porous biomaterials with micro-tubules.

literature_sources.citation: Krenchel, H. (1964). Fibre Reinforcement. Copenhagen: Akademisk Forlag.
literature_sources.reported_value: cos^4(theta) orientation efficiency factor for non-interacting aligned fiber composite

orientation_order.notes: Classical fiber orientation factor for axial load along orientation angle theta.

literature_sources.citation: Bertram, J. E., & Gosline, J. M. (1987). Functional design of horse hoof keratin: the modulation of mechanical properties through hydration effects. J. Exp. Biol., 130(1), 121-136.

strain_rate_sensitivity.notes: Logarithmic strain rate sensitivity factor (E proportional to (edot/edot0)^m).
